_comment: Registration, sign-in and the session. The session token is an HMAC-signed string in an httpOnly cookie - it is never readable by page scripts and never appears in a response body. It carries the user id and an expiry and DELIBERATELY NOT the role: every request re-reads the account, so a demotion takes effect on the next request rather than when the token expires.

register._comment: POST /api/auth/register. Everyone self-registers as a learner; only an admin can change a role afterwards, from the People screen.

password._comment: Minimum 8 characters. Sent once, hashed with scrypt and a per-account salt, then discarded.

login._comment: POST /api/auth/login. An account whose stored password is null is UNCLAIMED (migrated from before logins existed): the first sign-in sets the password instead of checking it.

me._comment: GET /api/auth/me - who the cookie says you are, and what that lets you reach. The client renders its navigation from this; the server enforces the same thing independently, because a hidden menu item is not a permission.

set_role._comment: PUT /api/people/:learner_id/role - admin only. Refused when it would remove the last admin, because recovering from that needs an operator to edit studio.config.json.

forgot._comment: POST /api/auth/forgot - step one. ALWAYS answers 200 with the same body, whether or not the account exists and whether or not it has an email. Saying 'no such account' here would turn this endpoint into a way to enumerate who is registered.

sent._comment: Always true. It means 'we have finished handling this', not 'an email left the building'.

reset._comment: POST /api/auth/reset - step two. Verifies the code against the stored digest and sets the new password. Does NOT sign the user in: they then sign in with the new password, which proves they know it.

password._comment: The new password. Minimum 8 characters, same rule as registration.

set_email._comment: PUT /api/people/:learner_id/email - admin only. Exists so accounts created before emails did are not permanently locked out of Forgot password.

logout._comment: POST /api/auth/logout - clears the cookie. There is no server-side session store to purge: the token is stateless and simply stops being sent.
